newsitem.title: USA: Dow industrials higher at midday, tech stocks soft.
newsitem.headline: Dow industrials higher at midday, tech stocks soft.

text.p: U.S. blue chip shares climbed slightly higher at midday on Monday, while technology stocks drifted at lower levels, as markets looked anxiously to a barrage of key economic data coming out later in the week.
The Dow Jones Industrial average, which staged a powerful advance last week after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan gave an upbeat testimony on the economy, made more modest gains on Monday.
It was up around 38 points at 8151, underpinned by strength in bonds and the dollar.
The Nasdaq composite, which had languished at lower levels for much of the morning session, recouped some ground to trade down 0.11 points at 1569.
The long bond added 12/32 to yield 6.44 percent. The dollar was also firm, trading at 1.8473/77 marks.

"The market is drifting here," said Charles White, managing director of Avatar Associates. "There are a bunch of economic numbers coming out this week...so investors are on the threshold, waiting for some more news to come out."

Greenspan lifted stocks and bonds last week by painting a rosy picture of the U.S. economy and calming fears of an imminent rate increase. But markets would look for further confirmation from this week's economic data, analysts said.
The second quarter employment cost index, due on Tuesday, would be scrutinized for any sign of a pickup in wage inflation, analysts said.
Later in the week, markets would shift their focus to the July employment report, due on Friday.
"We have some serious numbers coming out this week," said Pierre Ellis, senior economist at Primark Decision Economics.

"If it all adds up, the numbers could add credence to Greenspan's presentation," he said. "But if the employment cost index or the employment report are bad, it could be extremely disturbing to markets."

The employment cost index was forecast to rise 0.8 percent in the second quarter compared with a 0.6 percent gain in the previous quarter. The unemployment rate was seen declining to 4.9 percent in July from 5.0 percent in June.
"Though we have been up most of the day, the market is a little skittish," Jim Benning, a trader at BT Brokerage said.
"People are starting to wonder if the economy can get a whole lot better than it is now," he said. "Economic conditions have to stay exactly perfect for the market to stay at these kind of levels."

Technology stocks were mixed. Shares of personal computer makers were off lows, but still weak. They slipped after Bear Stearns analyst Andrew Neff downgraded Dell Computer Corp, voicing concerns over the stock's lofty valuations.
Dell was off 1-5/8 at 79-7/8, Compaq Computer Corp lost 3-3/16 to 132-1/4 and International Business Machines Corp was down 14/16 at 106-1/16.
Intel Corp firmed from a weaker open, trading up 3/16 to 89-3/8. The giant chipmaker said it planned to acquire Chips and Technologies Inc for $17.50 per share in cash, or about $384 million.
Chips and Technologies rose three points to 17.

General Motors Corp stock firmed two points to 58-7/8. Union workers voted to accept a contract at a key GM transmission and wheel plant, ending a four-day strike that threatened to paralyze all of GM's North American production.
((Wall Street desk 212-859-1730))
